# Introduction - what you are doing and why?

# 

This report provides a structured overview of thedevelopment process for The Lost Forest, a text-based adventure game. Startingfrom initial planning through to current implementation, it highlights how the
game was designed to deliver an interactive experience in which player choices
influence both the direction and outcome of the story. The branching narrative
lets players discover different storylines and endings, making the experience
more engaging and personal. The game combines elements such as combat, puzzles,
and item collection to make the adventure feel richer and more varied. These
features add layers of challenge and keep players coming back to try new ways.
Players can also save their progress and continue from the same point later.
The scoring system allows them to see their progress as they move through the
game. Development was carried out in C++, with mainly focusing on
object-oriented programming principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and
polymorphism. This approach supports modularity, reusability, and
maintainability of the code. Overall, the project demonstrates the practical
application of programming concepts in designing an interactive, console-based
game.

# Analysis and Design:

The program is a
text-based adventure game where the player progresses through different scenes
by choosing between two options. The main features of the program include:

- Binary choice system (option 1 or 2)
- Combat scenarios with health and attack
   system
- Puzzle scenarios such as riddles
- Inventory system to store items
- Score system to track player progress
- Save and load functionality using file
   handling

**Functional Requirements:**

The system must allow
players to enter their name at the beginning of the game which will be used
throughout the game. The system must present the player with two choices in
each scene and allow the player to select one option. The system must update
the game according to the player selection which will lead to changes in scenes
and health and score. The system must include different types of scenes which
include puzzle scenes and combat scenes and item collection scenes and basic
choice scenes. The system must evaluate player answers in puzzle scenes to
determine correct solutions while providing rewards or penalties. The system
must determine fight outcomes by calculating player and enemy power in combat
scenes. The system must allow players to collect items in item scenes while
their stats including attack and defence and health will be updated. The system
must keep track of player information which includes their health status and
number of lives and total score and items they possess. The system must show
the new player statistics and inventory items after every scene. The system
must include a scoring system which provides players with rewards for answering
questions correctly and winning battles and making accurate choices. The system
must enable players to save their progress through file handling and later
retrieve it. The system must keep player information which includes their name
and stats and inventory and current scene details in a storage file. The system
must perform player life checks while deducting lives from players whose health
reaches zero and terminating the game when players have no remaining lives.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**

The system requires
development through C++ programming language which needs to function properly
within the CLion integrated development environment. The program needs to
implement object-oriented programming principles through encapsulation and
inheritance and polymorphism to achieve structured and easily understandable
code.The system needs to provide user-friendly operation through its
straightforward user interface which enables simple input methods. The user
only needs to provide basic input through 1 or 2 while the program must repeat
the question when the user provides invalid input.The system needs to
demonstrate operational stability which prevents crashes throughout gaming
sessions. The system must incorporate error handling mechanisms which protect
against errors occurring during file reading and writing operations. The
program needs to execute without interruptions or performance delays.The system
needs to have design features which simplify maintenance tasks and support
future business growth. The system enables future development through its
implementation of classes and modular functions which support new scene and
feature deployment.The testing process needs to confirm all system features
function correctly which includes combat and puzzles and item collection and
saving and loading functions. The program needs to process edge cases which
include both invalid input and missing files.

## First stage: Outline program specification

The program created
for this assessment is a text-based adventure game called *The Lost Forest*.
In this game, the player moves through different scenes by choosing between two
options. Each choice leads to a different result. Some choices help the player
continue, while others may reduce health or end the game. The game includes
different features such as an inventory system, combat scenes, and puzzle
challenges. The player can collect items like weapons, food, and special
objects. These items help the player by increasing attack, defence, or health.
The game also includes a scoring system. The player earns points by solving
puzzles, winning fights, and making good decisions. In the final version of the
game, a save and load feature was added. This allows the player to save their
progress and continue later. The program is made using object-oriented
programming. Different classes are used to organise the program, such as
Player, Scene, and Inventory. Inheritance and polymorphism are used to manage
different types of scenes.

## Second stage: Identify inputs, outputs, and processes

| **Input**                  | **Process**                                  | **Output**                             |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Player name                | Stored at the start<br> and used in the game | Personalised<br> messages              |
| Player choice (1 or<br> 2) | Input is checked and<br> scene is updated    | New scene or result<br> shown          |
| Combat action              | Player and enemy<br> values are calculated   | Win or lose result,<br> health updated |
| Puzzle answer              | Answer is checked<br> with correct value     | Reward or penalty                      |
| Item choice                | Item is added and<br> stats are updated      | Inventory and stats<br> updated        |
| Save command               | Game data is written<br> to file             | Save confirmation<br> message          |
| Load command               | Game data is read<br> from file              | Game resumes from<br> saved point      |
| Player stats               | Health, score, and<br> lives updated         | Current status<br> displayed           |

## Technical Elements

The development of the program proceeded
through C++ programming language which used object-oriented programming design
principles for its execution. The system consists of multiple classes which
include Player, Scene, PuzzleScene, CombatScene, ItemScene, and GameSystem. The
program achieves better organization through this structure because it
simplifies code management and upcoming program extensions. The Player class
uses encapsulation to protect player health and score and inventory information
as private data which players can access through predefined methods. The system
uses inheritance to develop PuzzleScene and CombatScene and ItemScene from the
Scene class which enables developers to reuse existing code while avoiding code
duplication. The system employs polymorphism through the playScene() function
which creates different scene behaviors according to different scenarios. The
program uses vectors to store collections of scenes which enable programmers to
manage game data from dynamic sources. The program employs input and output
streams which use ifstream and ofstream methods to enable file handling
operations that support save and load functions. The program uses a text file
to store and retrieve player data which includes name health lives score current
scene and inventory items. The program includes error handling to verify file
opening success while protecting against system crashes that occur during
saving and loading processes. User input validation uses a function to verify
that users select valid choices between options 1 and 2. The program continues
to request user input until the user enters valid information which the program
accepts as correct. The design prevents the program from reaching an invalid
operational state. The combat system employs random number generation to create
unpredictable battle outcomes. The player's power gets calculated through his
attack and defense values along with a random value which he uses to compare
with the enemy's power for battle results. The inventory system uses boolean
variables to maintain information about which the system tracks.

# Evaluation

**Does it meet the program requirements?**

Overall, the text-based adventure game
meets the requirements set out in the brief. Players are able to make choices
at each stage, which shape how the story unfolds and lead to a different range
of possible outcomes, which mainly include being successful, others resulting
in health loss or game over. The game keeps things interesting by including
different types of scenarios, such as puzzles, combat, and item collection.
These features add variety and help make the gameplay more engaging. Players
can also collect items that impact their stats, like attack and defence, and a
scoring system is in place to reward those who solve puzzles or defeat enemies.
The ability to save and load progress makes it easy for players to step away
and resume the game at any time. However, a few areas still need improvement.
Input validation and inventory management are mostly working, but some
improvements can still be made to handle more edge cases and improve user
experience. While the main goals of the program have been achieved, some work
remains to fully meet all the requirements.

**Strengths of the program**

One of the program’s
main strengths is its use of object-oriented programming, which helps keep the
code organised into clear sections like player, scenes, and inventory. This
structure makes the game easier to manage and update. Another notable strength
is the variety in gameplay; the inclusion of puzzles, combat, and item
collection keeps things interesting and meets the requirement for different
scenarios. The inventory system is also a highlight, as players can collect
items that directly influence their stats and gameplay, showing that items have
a real impact on the overall experience.

**Weaknesses of the program**

One area where the
program could be slightly improved is input validation; some invalid inputs
aren’t always handled clearly, which might confuse players. Another weakness is
the simplicity of the story; while the game functions as intended, adding more detail
could make the experience more engaging. Additionally, the inventory system is
quite basic and currently lacks advanced features like using or removing items,
which would add more depth to gameplay.

**Areas for Improvement**

One way to enhance the
program would be to expand the story by adding more scenes and choices, which
would increase replay value and keep the players engaged. Improving input
validation is also important, so that any incorrect inputs are clearly addressed
with helpful error messages. Additionally, the inventory system could have been
made stronger by introducing features that allow players to use items during
gameplay.

**Issues encountered during testing**

Testing showed a few issues that needed attention. For instance, input
validation did not always catch incorrect values, so extra checks were added to
address this. There were also some problems with updating player stats and
inventory accurately, which were resolved after testing. Overall, the testing
process was essential for identifying these challenges and improving the
program’s functionality.

**Lessons learnt**

This project
highlighted the importance of thorough testing and debugging as key parts of
software development. Testing played an important role in discovering a few
issues, which could then be identified and resolved. I also learned that
object-oriented programming helps developers organise their code more
effectively and maintain better control over the project. By combining basic
functions with a well-structured design, the project was able to deliver a
functional system. However, early challenges occur with processing user input,
showing the need for careful input handling from the outset. If I were to
approach this project again, I would begin by creating a detailed blueprint
before starting to code. I would also dedicate more time to expanding the story,
adding new game features, and making the gameplay experience even more
interactive for players.

**Game_functions.cpp:**

*//  
// Created by Prithvi on 05-04-2026.  
//  

*#include "game_functions.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  
#include <fstream>  
#include <sstream>  

using
namespace std;  

vector<SceneText> LoadScenes(const string& filename)  
{    vector<SceneText> scenes;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        SceneText scene;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, '|');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        scene.id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, scene.title, '|');        getline(ss, scene.description, '|');        getline(ss, scene.choice1, '|');        getline(ss, scene.choice2, '|');        scenes.push_back(scene);  
    }    return scenes;  
}  

vector<PuzzleData> LoadPuzzles(const string& filename)  
{    vector<PuzzleData> puzzles;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        PuzzleData puzzle;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        puzzle.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, puzzle.question, ',');        getline(ss, puzzle.answer, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.reward_score = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.damage = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.heal = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, puzzle.item_reward, ',');        puzzles.push_back(puzzle);  
    }    return puzzles;  
}  

vector<CombatData> LoadCombat(const string& filename)  
{    vector<CombatData> combats;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        CombatData combat;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        combat.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, combat.enemy_name, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.enemy_base_power = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.damage_if_lose = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.reward_score = stoi(temp);        combats.push_back(combat);  
    }    return combats;  
}  

vector<ItemData> LoadItems(const string& filename)  
{    vector<ItemData> items;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        ItemData item;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        item.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, item.item_name, ',');        getline(ss, item.stat_type, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        item.stat_bonus = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        item.heal_bonus = stoi(temp);        items.push_back(item);  
    }    return items;  
}  

SceneText GetSceneById(const vector<SceneText>& scenes, int id)  
{    for (int i = 0; i < scenes.size(); i++)  
    {        if (scenes[i].id == id)  
        {            return scenes[i];  
        }  
    }    return {0, "Unknown", "Scene
not found.", "Choice 1", "Choice 2"};  
}  

PuzzleData GetPuzzleBySceneId(const vector<PuzzleData>& puzzles, int id)  
{    for (int i = 0; i < puzzles.size(); i++)  
    {        if (puzzles[i].scene_id == id)  
        {            return puzzles[i];  
        }  
    }    return {0, "", "", 0, 0, 0, "None"};  
}  

CombatData GetCombatBySceneId(const vector<CombatData>& combats, int id)  
{    for (int i = 0; i < combats.size(); i++)  
    {        if (combats[i].scene_id == id)  
        {            return combats[i];  
        }  
    }    return {0, "Unknown", 0, 0, 0};  
}  

ItemData GetItemBySceneId(const vector<ItemData>& items, int id)  
{    for (int i = 0; i < items.size(); i++)  
    {        if (items[i].scene_id == id)  
        {            return items[i];  
        }  
    }    return {0, "None", "none", 0, 0};  
}  

int ReadChoice12()  
{    string input;    while (true)  
    {        getline(cin, input);        if (input == "1") return 1;        if (input == "2") return 2;        cout << "Invalid input. Please enter 1 or 2: ";  
    }  
}  

void DisplayStats(int health, int lives, int score, int attack, int defense)  
{    cout << "\n----------- PLAYER STATS -----------\n";    cout << "Health  : " << health << endl;    cout << "Lives   : " << lives << endl;    cout << "Score   : " << score << endl;    cout << "Attack  : " << attack << endl;    cout << "Defense : " << defense << endl;  
}  

void DisplayInventory(bool has_hunters_dagger, bool has_healing_berries,                      bool has_cloak_of_thorns, bool has_ancient_amulet,                      bool has_fire_torch, bool has_enchanted_shield)  
{    cout << "\n---------- INVENTORY ----------\n";    bool has_items = false;    if (has_hunters_dagger)  
    {        cout << "- Hunter's Dagger\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (has_healing_berries)  
    {        cout << "- Healing Berries\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (has_cloak_of_thorns)  
    {        cout << "- Cloak of Thorns\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (has_ancient_amulet)  
    {        cout << "- Ancient Amulet\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (has_fire_torch)  
    {        cout << "- Fire Torch\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (has_enchanted_shield)  
    {        cout << "- Enchanted Shield\n";        has_items = true;  
    }    if (!has_items)  
    {        cout << "Empty\n";  
    }  
}  

void DisplayItemObtained(const string& item_name)  
{    cout << "\n******************************\n";    cout << "You have obtained: " << item_name << " *\n";    cout << "******************************\n";  
}  

bool CheckPlayerLife(int& health, int& lives)  
{    if (health <= 0)  
    {        lives--;        cout << "\nYou lost a life!\n";        if (lives <= 0)  
        {            cout << "\nGame Over\n";            return false;  
        }        health = 100;        cout << "Your health has been restored to 100.\n";  
    }    return true;  
}  

void SaveGame(const string& player_name, int health, int lives, int score,              int attack, int defense, int currentScene,              bool has_hunters_dagger, bool has_healing_berries,              bool has_cloak_of_thorns, bool has_ancient_amulet,              bool has_fire_torch, bool has_enchanted_shield)  
{    ofstream file("savegame.txt");    if (!file)  
    {        cout << "\nCould not save the game.\n";        return;  
    }    file << "Name=" << player_name         << ",Health=" << health         << ",Lives=" << lives         << ",Score=" << score         << ",Attack=" << attack         << ",Defense=" << defense         << ",CurrentScene=" << currentScene         << ",HuntersDagger=" << has_hunters_dagger         << ",HealingBerries=" << has_healing_berries         << ",CloakOfThorns=" << has_cloak_of_thorns         << ",AncientAmulet=" << has_ancient_amulet         << ",FireTorch=" << has_fire_torch         << ",EnchantedShield=" << has_enchanted_shield         << endl;    file.close();    cout << "\nGame saved successfully.\n";  
}  

bool LoadGame(string& player_name, int& health, int& lives, int& score,              int& attack, int& defense, int& currentScene,              bool& has_hunters_dagger, bool& has_healing_berries,              bool& has_cloak_of_thorns, bool& has_ancient_amulet,              bool& has_fire_torch, bool& has_enchanted_shield)  
{    ifstream file("savegame.txt");    if (!file)  
    {        cout << "\nNo saved game found.\n";        return false;  
    }    string line, lastLine;    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (!line.empty())  
        {            lastLine = line;  
        }  
    }    file.close();    if (lastLine.empty())  
    {        cout << "\nNo saved game data found.\n";        return false;  
    }    vector<string> parts;    string temp;    stringstream ss(lastLine);    while (getline(ss, temp, ','))  
    {        parts.push_back(temp);  
    }    if (parts.size() != 13)  
    {        cout << "\nSaved game format is invalid.\n";        return false;  
    }    auto getValue = [](string part) -> string    {        size_t pos = part.find('=');        if (pos != string::*npos*)  
        {            return part.substr(pos + 1);  
        }        return "";  
    };    player_name = getValue(parts[0]);    health = stoi(getValue(parts[1]));    lives = stoi(getValue(parts[2]));    score = stoi(getValue(parts[3]));    attack = stoi(getValue(parts[4]));    defense = stoi(getValue(parts[5]));    currentScene = stoi(getValue(parts[6]));    has_hunters_dagger = stoi(getValue(parts[7]));    has_healing_berries = stoi(getValue(parts[8]));    has_cloak_of_thorns = stoi(getValue(parts[9]));    has_ancient_amulet = stoi(getValue(parts[10]));    has_fire_torch = stoi(getValue(parts[11]));    has_enchanted_shield = stoi(getValue(parts[12]));    cout << "\nGame loaded successfully.\n";    return true;  
}

#include "Game.h"  
#include "ChoiceScene.h"  
#include "PuzzleScene.h"  
#include "ItemScene.h"  
#include "CombatScene.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  

using
namespace std;  

Game::Game()  
{    currentScene = 1;    scenes = LoadScenes("scenes.txt");    puzzles = LoadPuzzles("puzzles.csv");    combats = LoadCombat("combat.csv");    items = LoadItems("items.csv");    createScenes();  
}  

Game::~Game()  
{    for (int i = 0; i < sceneObjects.size(); i++)  
    {        delete sceneObjects[i];  
    }  
}  

void Game::createScenes()  
{    for (int i = 0; i < scenes.size(); i++)  
    {        int id = scenes[i].id;        if (id == 2 || id == 5 || id == 7 || id == 13 || id == 15 || id == 19)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new PuzzleScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else if (id == 3 || id == 6 || id == 9 || id == 11 || id == 17)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new ItemScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else if (id == 4 || id == 10 || id == 14 || id == 18 || id == 20 || id == 22 || id == 27)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new CombatScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new ChoiceScene(scenes[i]));  
        }  
    }  
}  

void Game::start()  
{    cout << "======= THE LOST FOREST GAME =======\n";    cout << "You awaken at the forest's edge with no
memory...\n";    cout << "A strange green mark glows softly on your
hand.\n";    string playerName;    cout << "\nEnter player name: ";    getline(cin, playerName);    player = Player(playerName);    cout << "\nWelcome to The Lost Forest, " << player.getName() << "!\n";    while (currentScene <= sceneObjects.size())  
    {        showMenu();  
    }    endGame();  
}  

void Game::showMenu()  
{    cout << "\n=========== GAME MENU ===========\n";    cout << "1. Continue\n";    cout << "2. Show Inventory\n";    cout << "3. Save Game\n";    cout << "4. Exit\n";    cout << "Choose: ";    string choice;    getline(cin, choice);    if (choice == "1")  
    {        continueGame();  
    }    else if (choice == "2")  
    {        showInventory();  
    }    else if (choice == "3")  
    {        saveGame();  
    }    else if (choice == "4")  
    {        saveGame();        cout << "Game saved. Exiting...\n";        exit(0);  
    }    else    {        cout << "Invalid input.\n";  
    }  
}  

void Game::continueGame()  
{    sceneObjects[currentScene - 1]->play(player, puzzles, combats, items);    currentScene++;  
}  

void Game::showInventory()  
{    DisplayInventory(player.getHuntersDagger(),                     player.getHealingBerries(),                     player.getCloakOfThorns(),                     player.getAncientAmulet(),                     player.getFireTorch(),                     player.getEnchantedShield());  
}  

void Game::saveGame()  
{    SaveGame(player.getName(),             player.getHealth(),             player.getLives(),             player.getScore(),             player.getAttack(),             player.getDefense(),             currentScene,             player.getHuntersDagger(),             player.getHealingBerries(),             player.getCloakOfThorns(),             player.getAncientAmulet(),             player.getFireTorch(),             player.getEnchantedShield());  
}  

void Game::endGame()  
{    cout << "\n======= THE LOST FOREST COMPLETE =======\n";    cout << "Final Score: " << player.getScore() << endl;    saveGame();    cout << "\nGame automatically saved at the end!\n";  
}

namespace std;  

void CombatScene::play(Player& player,                       const vector<PuzzleData>& puzzles,                       const vector<CombatData>& combats,                       const vector<ItemData>& items)  
{    CombatData combat = GetCombatBySceneId(combats, sceneText.id);    cout << "=== Scene " << sceneText.id << " -
" << sceneText.title << " ===\n";    cout << sceneText.description << "\n";    int player_roll = rand() % 6 + 1;    int enemy_roll = rand() % 6 + 1;    int player_power = player.getAttack() + player.getDefense() + player_roll;    int enemy_power = combat.enemy_base_power + enemy_roll;    cout << "\nYour combat power: " << player_power << endl;    cout << combat.enemy_name << " combat power: " << enemy_power << endl;    if (player_power >= enemy_power)  
    {        cout << "\nYou win the fight.\n";        player.setScore(player.getScore() + combat.reward_score);  
    }    else    {        cout << "\nYou lose the fight.\n";        player.setHealth(player.getHealth() - combat.damage_if_lose);  
    }    if (!CheckPlayerLife(player.healthRef(), player.livesRef()))  
    {        exit(0);  
    }    DisplayStats(player.getHealth(), player.getLives(), player.getScore(),                 player.getAttack(), player.getDefense());  
}

# Introduction - what you are doing and why?

# This report provides a structured overview of the

development process for The Lost Forest, a text-based adventure game. Starting
from initial planning through to current implementation, it highlights how the
game was designed to deliver an interactive experience in which player choices
influence both the direction and outcome of the story. The branching narrative
lets players discover different storylines and endings, making the experience
more engaging and personal. The game combines elements such as combat, puzzles,
and item collection to make the adventure feel richer and more varied. These
features add layers of challenge and keep players coming back to try new ways.
Players can also save their progress and continue from the same point later.
The scoring system allows them to see their progress as they move through the
game. Development was carried out in C++, with mainly focusing on
object-oriented programming principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and
polymorphism. This approach supports modularity, reusability, and
maintainability of the code. Overall, the project demonstrates the practical
application of programming concepts in designing an interactive, console-based
game.

# Analysis and Design:

The program is a
text-based adventure game where the player progresses through different scenes
by choosing between two options. The main features of the program include:

- Binary choice system (option 1 or 2)
- Combat scenarios with health and attack
   system
- Puzzle scenarios such as riddles
- Inventory system to store items
- Score system to track player progress
- Save and load functionality using file
   handling

**Functional Requirements:**

The system must allow
players to enter their name at the beginning of the game which will be used
throughout the game. The system must present the player with two choices in
each scene and allow the player to select one option. The system must update
the game according to the player selection which will lead to changes in scenes
and health and score. The system must include different types of scenes which
include puzzle scenes and combat scenes and item collection scenes and basic
choice scenes. The system must evaluate player answers in puzzle scenes to
determine correct solutions while providing rewards or penalties. The system
must determine fight outcomes by calculating player and enemy power in combat
scenes. The system must allow players to collect items in item scenes while
their stats including attack and defence and health will be updated. The system
must keep track of player information which includes their health status and
number of lives and total score and items they possess. The system must show
the new player statistics and inventory items after every scene. The system
must include a scoring system which provides players with rewards for answering
questions correctly and winning battles and making accurate choices. The system
must enable players to save their progress through file handling and later
retrieve it. The system must keep player information which includes their name
and stats and inventory and current scene details in a storage file. The system
must perform player life checks while deducting lives from players whose health
reaches zero and terminating the game when players have no remaining lives.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**

The system requires
development through C++ programming language which needs to function properly
within the CLion integrated development environment. The program needs to
implement object-oriented programming principles through encapsulation and
inheritance and polymorphism to achieve structured and easily understandable
code.The system needs to provide user-friendly operation through its
straightforward user interface which enables simple input methods. The user
only needs to provide basic input through 1 or 2 while the program must repeat
the question when the user provides invalid input.The system needs to
demonstrate operational stability which prevents crashes throughout gaming
sessions. The system must incorporate error handling mechanisms which protect
against errors occurring during file reading and writing operations. The
program needs to execute without interruptions or performance delays.The system
needs to have design features which simplify maintenance tasks and support
future business growth. The system enables future development through its
implementation of classes and modular functions which support new scene and
feature deployment.The testing process needs to confirm all system features
function correctly which includes combat and puzzles and item collection and
saving and loading functions. The program needs to process edge cases which
include both invalid input and missing files.

## First stage: Outline program specification

The program created
for this assessment is a text-based adventure game called *The Lost Forest*.
In this game, the player moves through different scenes by choosing between two
options. Each choice leads to a different result. Some choices help the player
continue, while others may reduce health or end the game. The game includes
different features such as an inventory system, combat scenes, and puzzle
challenges. The player can collect items like weapons, food, and special
objects. These items help the player by increasing attack, defence, or health.
The game also includes a scoring system. The player earns points by solving
puzzles, winning fights, and making good decisions. In the final version of the
game, a save and load feature was added. This allows the player to save their
progress and continue later. The program is made using object-oriented
programming. Different classes are used to organise the program, such as
Player, Scene, and Inventory. Inheritance and polymorphism are used to manage
different types of scenes.

## Technical Elements

The development of the program proceeded
through C++ programming language which used object-oriented programming design
principles for its execution. The system consists of multiple classes which
include Player, Scene, PuzzleScene, CombatScene, ItemScene, and GameSystem. The
program achieves better organization through this structure because it
simplifies code management and upcoming program extensions. The Player class
uses encapsulation to protect player health and score and inventory information
as private data which players can access through predefined methods. The system
uses inheritance to develop PuzzleScene and CombatScene and ItemScene from the
Scene class which enables developers to reuse existing code while avoiding code
duplication. The system employs polymorphism through the playScene() function
which creates different scene behaviors according to different scenarios. The
program uses vectors to store collections of scenes which enable programmers to
manage game data from dynamic sources. The program employs input and output
streams which use ifstream and ofstream methods to enable file handling
operations that support save and load functions. The program uses a text file
to store and retrieve player data which includes name health lives score current
scene and inventory items. The program includes error handling to verify file
opening success while protecting against system crashes that occur during
saving and loading processes. User input validation uses a function to verify
that users select valid choices between options 1 and 2. The program continues
to request user input until the user enters valid information which the program
accepts as correct. The design prevents the program from reaching an invalid
operational state. The combat system employs random number generation to create
unpredictable battle outcomes. The player's power gets calculated through his
attack and defense values along with a random value which he uses to compare
with the enemy's power for battle results. The inventory system uses boolean
variables to maintain information about which the system tracks.

# Evaluation

**Does it meet the program requirements?**

Overall, the text-based adventure game
meets the requirements set out in the brief. Players are able to make choices
at each stage, which shape how the story unfolds and lead to a different range
of possible outcomes, which mainly include being successful, others resulting
in health loss or game over. The game keeps things interesting by including
different types of scenarios, such as puzzles, combat, and item collection.
These features add variety and help make the gameplay more engaging. Players
can also collect items that impact their stats, like attack and defence, and a
scoring system is in place to reward those who solve puzzles or defeat enemies.
The ability to save and load progress makes it easy for players to step away
and resume the game at any time. However, a few areas still need improvement.
Input validation and inventory management are mostly working, but some
improvements can still be made to handle more edge cases and improve user
experience. While the main goals of the program have been achieved, some work
remains to fully meet all the requirements.

**Strengths of the program**

One of the program’s
main strengths is its use of object-oriented programming, which helps keep the
code organised into clear sections like player, scenes, and inventory. This
structure makes the game easier to manage and update. Another notable strength
is the variety in gameplay; the inclusion of puzzles, combat, and item
collection keeps things interesting and meets the requirement for different
scenarios. The inventory system is also a highlight, as players can collect
items that directly influence their stats and gameplay, showing that items have
a real impact on the overall experience.

**Weaknesses of the program**

One area where the
program could be slightly improved is input validation; some invalid inputs
aren’t always handled clearly, which might confuse players. Another weakness is
the simplicity of the story; while the game functions as intended, adding more detail
could make the experience more engaging. Additionally, the inventory system is
quite basic and currently lacks advanced features like using or removing items,
which would add more depth to gameplay.

**Areas for Improvement**

One way to enhance the
program would be to expand the story by adding more scenes and choices, which
would increase replay value and keep the players engaged. Improving input
validation is also important, so that any incorrect inputs are clearly addressed
with helpful error messages. Additionally, the inventory system could have been
made stronger by introducing features that allow players to use items during
gameplay.

**Issues encountered during testing**

Testing showed a few issues that needed attention. For instance, input
validation did not always catch incorrect values, so extra checks were added to
address this. There were also some problems with updating player stats and
inventory accurately, which were resolved after testing. Overall, the testing
process was essential for identifying these challenges and improving the
program’s functionality.

**Lessons learnt**

This project
highlighted the importance of thorough testing and debugging as key parts of
software development. Testing played an important role in discovering a few
issues, which could then be identified and resolved. I also learned that
object-oriented programming helps developers organise their code more
effectively and maintain better control over the project. By combining basic
functions with a well-structured design, the project was able to deliver a
functional system. However, early challenges occur with processing user input,
showing the need for careful input handling from the outset. If I were to
approach this project again, I would begin by creating a detailed blueprint
before starting to code. I would also dedicate more time to expanding the story,
adding new game features, and making the gameplay experience even more
interactive for players.

vector<SceneText> LoadScenes(const string& filename)  
{    vector<SceneText> scenes;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        SceneText scene;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, '|');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        scene.id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, scene.title, '|');        getline(ss, scene.description, '|');        getline(ss, scene.choice1, '|');        getline(ss, scene.choice2, '|');        scenes.push_back(scene);  
    }    return scenes;  
}  

vector<PuzzleData> LoadPuzzles(const string& filename)  
{    vector<PuzzleData> puzzles;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        PuzzleData puzzle;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        puzzle.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, puzzle.question, ',');        getline(ss, puzzle.answer, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.reward_score = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.damage = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        puzzle.heal = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, puzzle.item_reward, ',');        puzzles.push_back(puzzle);  
    }    return puzzles;  
}  

vector<CombatData> LoadCombat(const string& filename)  
{    vector<CombatData> combats;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        CombatData combat;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        combat.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, combat.enemy_name, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.enemy_base_power = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.damage_if_lose = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        combat.reward_score = stoi(temp);        combats.push_back(combat);  
    }    return combats;  
}  

vector<ItemData> LoadItems(const string& filename)  
{    vector<ItemData> items;    ifstream file(filename);    string line;    getline(file, line);    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (line.empty()) continue;        stringstream ss(line);        ItemData item;        string temp;        getline(ss, temp, ',');        if (temp.empty()) continue;        item.scene_id = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, item.item_name, ',');        getline(ss, item.stat_type, ',');        getline(ss, temp, ',');        item.stat_bonus = stoi(temp);        getline(ss, temp, ',');        item.heal_bonus = stoi(temp);        items.push_back(item);  
    }    return items;  
}

not found.", "Choice 1", "Choice 2"};

bool CheckPlayerLife(int& health, int& lives)  
{    if (health <= 0)  
    {        lives--;        cout << "\nYou lost a life!\n";        if (lives <= 0)  
        {            cout << "\nGame Over\n";            return false;  
        }        health = 100;        cout << "Your health has been restored to 100.\n";  
    }    return true;  
}  

void SaveGame(const string& player_name, int health, int lives, int score,              int attack, int defense, int currentScene,              bool has_hunters_dagger, bool has_healing_berries,              bool has_cloak_of_thorns, bool has_ancient_amulet,              bool has_fire_torch, bool has_enchanted_shield)  
{    ofstream file("savegame.txt");    if (!file)  
    {        cout << "\nCould not save the game.\n";        return;  
    }    file << "Name=" << player_name         << ",Health=" << health         << ",Lives=" << lives         << ",Score=" << score         << ",Attack=" << attack         << ",Defense=" << defense         << ",CurrentScene=" << currentScene         << ",HuntersDagger=" << has_hunters_dagger         << ",HealingBerries=" << has_healing_berries         << ",CloakOfThorns=" << has_cloak_of_thorns         << ",AncientAmulet=" << has_ancient_amulet         << ",FireTorch=" << has_fire_torch         << ",EnchantedShield=" << has_enchanted_shield         << endl;    file.close();    cout << "\nGame saved successfully.\n";  
}  

bool LoadGame(string& player_name, int& health, int& lives, int& score,              int& attack, int& defense, int& currentScene,              bool& has_hunters_dagger, bool& has_healing_berries,              bool& has_cloak_of_thorns, bool& has_ancient_amulet,              bool& has_fire_torch, bool& has_enchanted_shield)  
{    ifstream file("savegame.txt");    if (!file)  
    {        cout << "\nNo saved game found.\n";        return false;  
    }    string line, lastLine;    while (getline(file, line))  
    {        if (!line.empty())  
        {            lastLine = line;  
        }  
    }    file.close();    if (lastLine.empty())  
    {        cout << "\nNo saved game data found.\n";        return false;  
    }    vector<string> parts;    string temp;    stringstream ss(lastLine);    while (getline(ss, temp, ','))  
    {        parts.push_back(temp);  
    }    if (parts.size() != 13)  
    {        cout << "\nSaved game format is invalid.\n";        return false;  
    }    auto getValue = [](string part) -> string    {        size_t pos = part.find('=');        if (pos != string::*npos*)  
        {            return part.substr(pos + 1);  
        }        return "";  
    };    player_name = getValue(parts[0]);    health = stoi(getValue(parts[1]));    lives = stoi(getValue(parts[2]));    score = stoi(getValue(parts[3]));    attack = stoi(getValue(parts[4]));    defense = stoi(getValue(parts[5]));    currentScene = stoi(getValue(parts[6]));    has_hunters_dagger = stoi(getValue(parts[7]));    has_healing_berries = stoi(getValue(parts[8]));    has_cloak_of_thorns = stoi(getValue(parts[9]));    has_ancient_amulet = stoi(getValue(parts[10]));    has_fire_torch = stoi(getValue(parts[11]));    has_enchanted_shield = stoi(getValue(parts[12]));    cout << "\nGame loaded successfully.\n";    return true;  
}

#include "Game.h"  
#include "ChoiceScene.h"  
#include "PuzzleScene.h"  
#include "ItemScene.h"  
#include "CombatScene.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  

using
namespace std;  

Game::Game()  
{    currentScene = 1;    scenes = LoadScenes("scenes.txt");    puzzles = LoadPuzzles("puzzles.csv");    combats = LoadCombat("combat.csv");    items = LoadItems("items.csv");    createScenes();  
}  

Game::~Game()  
{    for (int i = 0; i < sceneObjects.size(); i++)  
    {        delete sceneObjects[i];  
    }  
}  

void Game::createScenes()  
{    for (int i = 0; i < scenes.size(); i++)  
    {        int id = scenes[i].id;        if (id == 2 || id == 5 || id == 7 || id == 13 || id == 15 || id == 19)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new PuzzleScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else if (id == 3 || id == 6 || id == 9 || id == 11 || id == 17)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new ItemScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else if (id == 4 || id == 10 || id == 14 || id == 18 || id == 20 || id == 22 || id == 27)  
        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new CombatScene(scenes[i]));  
        }        else        {            sceneObjects.push_back(new ChoiceScene(scenes[i]));  
        }  
    }  
}  

void Game::start()  
{    cout << "======= THE LOST FOREST GAME =======\n";    cout << "You awaken at the forest's edge with no
memory...\n";    cout << "A strange green mark glows softly on your
hand.\n";    string playerName;    cout << "\nEnter player name: ";    getline(cin, playerName);    player = Player(playerName);    cout << "\nWelcome to The Lost Forest, " << player.getName() << "!\n";    while (currentScene <= sceneObjects.size())  
    {        showMenu();  
    }    endGame();  
}  

void Game::showMenu()  
{    cout << "\n=========== GAME MENU ===========\n";    cout << "1. Continue\n";    cout << "2. Show Inventory\n";    cout << "3. Save Game\n";    cout << "4. Exit\n";    cout << "Choose: ";    string choice;    getline(cin, choice);    if (choice == "1")  
    {        continueGame();  
    }    else if (choice == "2")  
    {        showInventory();  
    }    else if (choice == "3")  
    {        saveGame();  
    }    else if (choice == "4")  
    {        saveGame();        cout << "Game saved. Exiting...\n";        exit(0);  
    }    else    {        cout << "Invalid input.\n";  
    }  
}  

void Game::continueGame()  
{    sceneObjects[currentScene - 1]->play(player, puzzles, combats, items);    currentScene++;  
}  

void Game::showInventory()  
{    DisplayInventory(player.getHuntersDagger(),                     player.getHealingBerries(),                     player.getCloakOfThorns(),                     player.getAncientAmulet(),                     player.getFireTorch(),                     player.getEnchantedShield());  
}  

void Game::saveGame()  
{    SaveGame(player.getName(),             player.getHealth(),             player.getLives(),             player.getScore(),             player.getAttack(),             player.getDefense(),             currentScene,             player.getHuntersDagger(),             player.getHealingBerries(),             player.getCloakOfThorns(),             player.getAncientAmulet(),             player.getFireTorch(),             player.getEnchantedShield());  
}  

void Game::endGame()  
{    cout << "\n======= THE LOST FOREST COMPLETE =======\n";    cout << "Final Score: " << player.getScore() << endl;    saveGame();    cout << "\nGame automatically saved at the end!\n";  
}

#ifndef GAME_H

#include "ChoiceScene.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  

using
namespace std;  

void ChoiceScene::play(Player& player,                       const vector<PuzzleData>& puzzles,                       const vector<CombatData>& combats,                       const vector<ItemData>& items)  
{    cout << "=== Scene " << sceneText.id << " -
" << sceneText.title << " ===\n";    cout << sceneText.description << "\n";    cout << "1) " << sceneText.choice1 << "\n";    cout << "2) " << sceneText.choice2 << "\n";    cout << "Enter your choice (1 or 2): ";    int choice = ReadChoice12();    if (choice == 1)  
    {        cout << "\nYou chose option 1.\n";        player.setScore(player.getScore() + 10);  
    }    else    {        cout << "\nYou chose option 2.\n";        player.setHealth(player.getHealth() - 10);  
    }    if (!CheckPlayerLife(player.healthRef(), player.livesRef()))  
    {        exit(0);  
    }    DisplayStats(player.getHealth(), player.getLives(), player.getScore(),                 player.getAttack(), player.getDefense());  
}

**PuzzleScene.cpp:**

#include "PuzzleScene.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  

using
namespace std;  

void PuzzleScene::play(Player& player,                       const vector<PuzzleData>& puzzles,                       const vector<CombatData>& combats,                       const vector<ItemData>& items)  
{    PuzzleData puzzle = GetPuzzleBySceneId(puzzles, sceneText.id);    cout << "=== Scene " << sceneText.id << " -
" << sceneText.title << " ===\n";    cout << sceneText.description << "\n";    cout << puzzle.question << "\n";    cout << "Enter your answer: ";    string answer;    getline(cin, answer);    if (answer == puzzle.answer)  
    {        cout << "\nCorrect!\n";        player.setScore(player.getScore() + puzzle.reward_score);  
    }    else    {        cout << "\nWrong answer!\n";        player.setHealth(player.getHealth() - puzzle.damage);  
    }    if (!CheckPlayerLife(player.healthRef(), player.livesRef()))  
    {        exit(0);  
    }    DisplayStats(player.getHealth(), player.getLives(), player.getScore(),                 player.getAttack(), player.getDefense());  
}

            }

            {                player.setAncientAmulet(true);                player.setAttack(player.getAttack() + item.stat_bonus);                player.setDefense(player.getDefense() + item.stat_bonus);                DisplayItemObtained(item.item_name);  
            }            else            {                cout << "You
already have the Ancient Amulet.\n";  
            }  
        }        else if (item.item_name == "Fire

        {            if (!player.getFireTorch())

            }

            }  
        }        player.setScore(player.getScore() + 10);  
    }    else    {        cout << "\nYou move on.\n";  
    }    DisplayStats(player.getHealth(), player.getLives(), player.getScore(),                 player.getAttack(), player.getDefense());  
}

**CombatScene.cpp:**

#include "CombatScene.h"  
#include <iostream>  
#include
<cstdlib>  

using
namespace std;  

void CombatScene::play(Player& player,                       const vector<PuzzleData>& puzzles,                       const vector<CombatData>& combats,                       const vector<ItemData>& items)  
{    CombatData combat = GetCombatBySceneId(combats, sceneText.id);    cout << "=== Scene " << sceneText.id << " -
" << sceneText.title << " ===\n";    cout << sceneText.description << "\n";    int player_roll = rand() % 6 + 1;    int enemy_roll = rand() % 6 + 1;    int player_power = player.getAttack() + player.getDefense() + player_roll;    int enemy_power = combat.enemy_base_power + enemy_roll;    cout << "\nYour combat power: " << player_power << endl;    cout << combat.enemy_name << " combat power: " << enemy_power << endl;    if (player_power >= enemy_power)  
    {        cout << "\nYou win the fight.\n";        player.setScore(player.getScore() + combat.reward_score);  
    }    else    {        cout << "\nYou lose the fight.\n";        player.setHealth(player.getHealth() - combat.damage_if_lose);  
    }    if (!CheckPlayerLife(player.healthRef(), player.livesRef()))  
    {        exit(0);  
    }    DisplayStats(player.getHealth(), player.getLives(), player.getScore(),                 player.getAttack(), player.getDefense());  
}
